items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Productive labour.
o: the excess of what buyers would have been willing to pay over what they actually hand over
work that adds to the stock of goods available for use at a later date
the taking of a charge for lending, condemned by medieval church teaching as wrongful gain
the writer who tried to join classical production theory with a reformed view of distribution
items.s: Productive labour: work that adds to the stock of goods available for use at a later date. The other options describe John Stuart Mill, Usury, Consumer surplus.
items.t: Adam Smith and the classical school

items.q: Which of the following best describes Subsistence wage?

the engineer turned economist whose test accepts a change only when nobody is left worse off
a structure in which a modern high-yield sector coexists with a traditional sector of low yield
pay no higher than is needed to keep a worker and family alive and working
items.s: Subsistence wage: pay no higher than is needed to keep a worker and family alive and working. The other options describe General equilibrium, Vilfredo Pareto, Dual economy.

items.q: Milton Friedman may be defined as

items.q: The statement “the habit of forecasting future conditions from the recent past alone” describes which of the following?

items.s: Old institutionalism: the approach that treats habits, rules and organisations, not isolated choosers, as the proper subject. The other options describe Conspicuous consumption, Thorstein Veblen, Creative destruction.

items.q: Three of these relate to Welfare economics and imperfect competition. Which one does not?
o: Welfare economics
External effect
Aristotle
Arthur Pigou
items.s: Every other option belongs to Welfare economics and imperfect competition. “Aristotle” belongs to Ancient, medieval and Islamic ideas, not Welfare economics and imperfect competition.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Positive check.
o: the rise in deaths through want and disease that pulls numbers back to the food available
the fall in the extra output obtained when more of one input is applied to a fixed quantity of another
pay no higher than is needed to keep a worker and family alive and working
the rule that a country gains by specialising where its relative cost of production is lowest
items.s: Positive check: the rise in deaths through want and disease that pulls numbers back to the food available. The other options describe Subsistence wage, Comparative advantage, Diminishing returns.

items.q: In this course, Dual economy refers to
o: the Austrian economist who made the innovating business leader the engine of economic change
a structure in which a modern high-yield sector coexists with a traditional sector of low yield
spending on goods chiefly in order to display wealth and standing
the claim that poorer nations remain poor because their surplus is drawn away by richer ones
items.s: Dual economy: a structure in which a modern high-yield sector coexists with a traditional sector of low yield. The other options describe Dependency theory, Joseph Schumpeter, Conspicuous consumption.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Invisible hand?
o: the amount just enough to cover the ordinary costs of production together with normal profit
the claim that self-seeking exchange under competition guides resources to their most valued uses
commerce between nations left unhindered by tariffs, quotas and prohibitions
the amount actually paid at a given moment, which may stand above or below the ordinary cost of supply
items.s: Invisible hand: the claim that self-seeking exchange under competition guides resources to their most valued uses. The other options describe Natural price, Free trade, Market price.
items.t: Adam Smith and the classical school

items.q: Laissez-faire may be defined as
o: the surplus left over in farming after the costs of cultivation have been met
the rule that exports should exceed imports so that treasure flows into the country
the counsel that government should leave trade and industry to settle themselves
the narrower belief that wealth consists chiefly in the accumulation of gold and silver
items.s: Laissez-faire: the counsel that government should leave trade and industry to settle themselves. The other options describe Balance of trade doctrine, Bullionism, Net product.

items.q: “the amount actually paid at a given moment, which may stand above or below the ordinary cost of supply” is the definition of
o: Market price
Wealth of Nations
Unproductive labour
Free trade
items.s: Market price is the amount actually paid at a given moment, which may stand above or below the ordinary cost of supply.
items.t: Adam Smith and the classical school

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Marginal efficiency of capital.
o: a settled position in which output and jobs stay below capacity because spending is too low
the readiness to vary taxes and public works deliberately in order to manage total demand
the book that recast output and jobs as determined by the level of total spending
the expected yield of an extra unit of equipment set against the cost of the funds needed to buy it
items.s: Marginal efficiency of capital: the expected yield of an extra unit of equipment set against the cost of the funds needed to buy it. The other options describe Underemployment equilibrium, General Theory, Fiscal activism.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Rational expectations.
o: the proposition that the general price level moves with the stock of circulating means of payment
the body of work that rebuilt macroeconomics on markets assumed to clear continuously
the assumption that people forecast with all available information and do not repeat systematic error
the habit of forecasting future conditions from the recent past alone

items.q: Oikonomia may be defined as
o: the church lawyers who framed rules on lending, pricing and fair dealing in exchange
the Greek expression for the management of a household, from which the modern name of the discipline is derived
the Greek philosopher who separated the use of goods from their acquisition for gain and doubted the latter
the taking of a charge for lending, condemned by medieval church teaching as wrongful gain
items.s: Oikonomia: the Greek expression for the management of a household, from which the modern name of the discipline is derived. The other options describe Usury, Aristotle, Canonists.

items.q: Surplus value may be defined as
o: the view that the way goods are produced drives changes in law, politics and belief
the recurring conflict between those who own productive property and those who must sell their effort
the portion of the product that the owner of an enterprise keeps beyond what the hired worker is paid
the work that analysed the production and circulation of capital as a social relation of exploitation
items.s: Surplus value: the portion of the product that the owner of an enterprise keeps beyond what the hired worker is paid. The other options describe Das Kapital, Historical materialism, Class struggle.

items.q: In this course, Joan Robinson refers to
o: the Cambridge economist who argued that private choices ignore costs and benefits that fall on others
the Cambridge writer who showed how a seller facing a falling demand curve restricts output
a gain or loss that falls on people who were not party to the decision that produced it
the case in which uncoordinated private dealings cannot deliver an efficient use of resources
items.s: Joan Robinson: the Cambridge writer who showed how a seller facing a falling demand curve restricts output. The other options describe Market failure, Arthur Pigou, External effect.

items.q: Tableau Economique may be defined as
o: a circular diagram showing how spending passes between farmers, landowners and artisans
the surplus left over in farming after the costs of cultivation have been met
the counsel that government should leave trade and industry to settle themselves
the narrower belief that wealth consists chiefly in the accumulation of gold and silver

items.q: Division of labour may be defined as
o: the amount just enough to cover the ordinary costs of production together with normal profit
the book that set out how a country's yearly output is produced, distributed and made to grow
the claim that self-seeking exchange under competition guides resources to their most valued uses
the splitting of production into narrow tasks so that each worker repeats a single operation

items.t: Adam Smith and the classical school

items.q: The correct meaning of Rational expectations is
o: the assumption that people forecast with all available information and do not repeat systematic error
the body of work that rebuilt macroeconomics on markets assumed to clear continuously
the proposition that the general price level moves with the stock of circulating means of payment
the Chicago economist who doubted that authorities could time their interventions better than the market
items.s: Rational expectations: the assumption that people forecast with all available information and do not repeat systematic error. The other options describe Quantity theory of money, Milton Friedman, New classical economics.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the rule that a country gains by specialising where its relative cost of production is lowest”
o: Positive check
Subsistence wage
Comparative advantage
Diminishing returns
items.s: Comparative advantage is the rule that a country gains by specialising where its relative cost of production is lowest.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Free trade?
o: work that yields a service enjoyed at the moment and leaves nothing behind
commerce between nations left unhindered by tariffs, quotas and prohibitions
the splitting of production into narrow tasks so that each worker repeats a single operation
the book that set out how a country's yearly output is produced, distributed and made to grow
items.s: Free trade: commerce between nations left unhindered by tariffs, quotas and prohibitions. The other options describe Division of labour, Unproductive labour, Wealth of Nations.
items.t: Adam Smith and the classical school

items.q: The correct meaning of Rent is
o: the delay of marriage and restraint within it that keeps births below the food limit
the sum earned by a landowner because the soil yields more than the margin needed to bring the poorest land into use
the claim that numbers tend to grow faster than the food supply unless restraint intervenes
the fall in the extra output obtained when more of one input is applied to a fixed quantity of another

items.q: In this course, Scholastic method refers to
o: the taking of a charge for lending, condemned by medieval church teaching as wrongful gain
the style of reasoning in medieval universities that tried to reconcile received faith with argument
the Greek expression for the management of a household, from which the modern name of the discipline is derived
the church lawyers who framed rules on lending, pricing and fair dealing in exchange
items.s: Scholastic method: the style of reasoning in medieval universities that tried to reconcile received faith with argument. The other options describe Oikonomia, Canonists, Usury.

items.q: In this course, New classical economics refers to
o: the assumption that people forecast with all available information and do not repeat systematic error
the habit of forecasting future conditions from the recent past alone
the body of work that rebuilt macroeconomics on markets assumed to clear continuously
the joblessness that persists once the upturn and the downturn have been averaged out
items.s: New classical economics: the body of work that rebuilt macroeconomics on markets assumed to clear continuously. The other options describe Rational expectations, Natural rate of unemployment, Adaptive expectations.

items.q: In this course, Monopolistic competition refers to
o: the Cambridge economist who argued that private choices ignore costs and benefits that fall on others
a market of many sellers whose products are close substitutes but not identical
the situation in which at least one seller can influence the price of what it offers
the case in which uncoordinated private dealings cannot deliver an efficient use of resources

items.q: Usury may be defined as

the church lawyers who framed rules on lending, pricing and fair dealing in exchange
the style of reasoning in medieval universities that tried to reconcile received faith with argument
the taking of a charge for lending, condemned by medieval church teaching as wrongful gain

the Greek philosopher who separated the use of goods from their acquisition for gain and doubted the latter
the style of reasoning in medieval universities that tried to reconcile received faith with argument

the rule that a country gains by specialising where its relative cost of production is lowest

New classical economics
Quantity theory of money

the splitting of production into narrow tasks so that each worker repeats a single operation
commerce between nations left unhindered by tariffs, quotas and prohibitions
work that yields a service enjoyed at the moment and leaves nothing behind

o: Saint-Simon
Utopian socialism
John Stuart Mill
Charles Fourier

items.q: Alfred Marshall may be defined as

the shift that explained worth by the satisfaction gained from the last unit rather than by effort embodied
the Swiss economist who modelled all markets together as a set of simultaneous equations
the Cambridge teacher who organised price theory around the crossing of demand and supply for one market
